subject: The 28 in-scope Mermaid Fidelity capability assessments (basis `model-concept`) that no recorded review confirmed under scoring v3's exact-reason matching (unified/mermaid-fidelity/verification.ts): after the 2026-11-14 capability and model-concept reviews, these callbacks' reasons matched no `confirmed` entry. Projects: Dicklesworthstone/frankenmermaid 0.5.0 (3), Latias94/merman 0.10.0 (9), adewale/agentic-mermaid 0.5.6 (13), evangwt/xmermaid 0.4.2 (1), lukilabs/beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 (1), kais-radwan/ascii-mermaid 0.1.0 (1).
baseline: The 2026-11-15 jsdom Fidelity run (prepared artifacts of the 2026-11-14 campaign, community-prepared.json) recounted under scoring v3 with fidelity-capability-review-2026-11-14.json and fidelity-model-concept-review-2026-11-14.json: baselineCallbacks counts, per project, the in-scope reference-passing callbacks whose capability assessment carried that reason and was unconfirmed.
method: Each concept was probed again by running the candidate's own installed parser through the runtime's native parse path exactly as the views receive it (runtime.ts probeNative, as scripts/fidelity-probe.ts does; several sources per runtime), on the test's own source and on sources that differ only in the concept (probeSources below), then comparing the models; installed type declarations and Mermaid's own database code were read where a verdict depends on them (cited file:line). Confirmed: the native model does not carry what the test reads (dropped, folded, merged with another written form, or kept only as raw source text). Disproved: the native model carries it, so the view must read it. Not decidable: the probe cannot settle the claim. Reasons are keyed by the verdict text exactly as the run records it, every number written as N.
finding: All eight concepts had already been probed and confirmed or narrowed by the 2026-11-14 review; their callbacks stayed unconfirmed because that review keyed reasons cut at 160 characters (Frankenmermaid activations, Latias94/merman railroad and agentflow, agentic-mermaid opaque blocks, XMermaid cross-document transitions), keyed them under another project's name (beautiful-mermaid and ascii-mermaid under zombie-mermaid) or measured a narrowed reason without keying it (agentic-mermaid class-style merge and animate: false). Every concept was re-probed here rather than carried over.
measured: No view changed: no concept was disproved. With this file added to the two 2026-11-14 review files, the recount of the same run leaves 0 in-scope capability assessments unconfirmed (28 before).

concepts.evidence: Frankenmermaid 0.5.0 (WASM IR, sequence_meta.activations) keeps only { participant, start_edge, end_edge, depth }. `Alice-->>Bob / activate Bob / Bob-->>Alice / deactivate Bob` and `Alice-->>+Bob / Bob-->>-Alice` give identical IRs apart from edge spans ({ participant: 1, start_edge: 0, end_edge: 1 }), so no message records the +/- marker Mermaid stores as message.activate (read by 'one line notation activation'). An activation never closed ends at the last edge: `A->>+B / B->>A / A->>B` and the same with a trailing `deactivate B` both give end_edge 2, and `Alice-->>+Bob / Bob-->>Alice` gives the same range as the closed `Bob-->>-Alice`, so whether Mermaid's ACTIVE_END after the last message exists (read by 'actor activation' and 'stacked activations', whose activations all close on the last message) is not recorded. An `activate Bob` written before the first message leaves no activation at all. Only edge span line numbers differ, which is source layout, not an activation record (and `;` separators break even that).
concepts.action: Kept (frankenmermaid.mjs sequence view). The 2026-11-14 review (seq-activation) confirmed this concept but keyed the reason cut at 160 characters, so no callback matched it under exact-text matching.

concepts.evidence: merman-cli 0.10.0 `parse` keeps Mermaid's railroad database record (railroadParser.ts transformExpression: a one-element sequence(...) or choice(...) returns its element). `one = sequence(terminal("a"))` and `bare = terminal("a")` both give { type: 'terminal', value: 'a' }; `choice(special("x"))` gives { type: 'special' }; `sequence(optional(terminal("a")))` gives the same optional record as `optional(terminal("a"))`. A sequence or choice record does not settle the written type either: `w = choice(sequence(terminal("a"), nonterminal("b")))` gives the same { type: 'sequence', elements: [terminal, nonterminal] } as `sequence(terminal("a"), nonterminal("b"))`, and `sequence(choice(a, b, c))` the same choice record as `choice(a, b, c)`. So no record node determines the Langium $type the four tests read (RailroadSequenceExpr / ChoiceExpr / OptionalExpr / OneOrMoreExpr / ZeroOrMoreExpr / SpecialExpr, and element $types). Pele 1.13.0 and Bezel 0.2.26 give the same records for both probes.
concepts.action: Kept (ports.mjs railroadAst). The 2026-11-14 review (railroad-fold) confirmed it, but its Latias94/merman key was cut at 160 characters and did not match.

concepts.evidence: merman-cli 0.10.0 `parse --meta` (the bridge's interface) for `a["A"]@{ icon: "fa:bell", form: circle, description: "DESCX" }`, `c["C"]@{ img: "https://example.com/x.png", w: 40, h: 40 }`, `b["B"]@{}` and `pipeline@{ view: "collapsed" }`: vertex a has metadata { description: 'DESCX' } only, c and b have no metadata key, the subgraph record { id, title, nodes, type } has no metadata; none of fa:bell, circle, example.com, 40-sized w/h or collapsed occurs anywhere in the model. `a@{ __proto__: ... }` leaves a with no metadata key, the same as a vertex with presentation keys or with none, so neither the metadata objects the four vertex tests compare nor the subgraph's metadata.view is recoverable. merman-cli `layout` output for the same source also carries none of these values.
concepts.action: Kept (ports.mjs agentflow view). The 2026-11-14 review (agentflow-latias) confirmed it, but its key was cut at 160 characters and did not match.

concepts.evidence: agentic-mermaid 0.5.6 class model: `class Class01:::pink / classDef pink fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:6px` and the same two statements in the other order give identical models (classes[0].className 'pink', classDefs.pink { fill, stroke, stroke-width }), but Mermaid's styles differ: classDb.ts defineClass (lines 363-367) appends a classDef's styles only to classes that already carry the class, and setCssClass (331-342) appends the class name without styles, so the first gives ['fill:#f9f', 'stroke:#333', 'stroke-width:6px'] and the second []. With `cssClass "Class01" bold` added the model keeps className 'bold' alone (pink is lost), so neither the merged styles nor cssClasses 'default pink bold' are recorded.
concepts.action: Kept (misc.mjs agenticClassModel). The 2026-11-14 review (agentic-class-styles) disproved the older reason (no per-class styles) and narrowed the reading to this reason, which it measured but did not key.

concepts.evidence: agentic-mermaid 0.5.6 SequenceBody (dist/paint-certification-aIPtFDcn.d.ts:3481-3520): statements are participant, message, fragment or { kind: 'opaque-block', lines }. Each of the ten test sources parses with the listed lines as one opaque-block of raw source text: rect and nested rects, critical with and without options, break, par_over holding notes (SequenceFragment branches hold messages only), and alt / par whose labels carry `;` separators and `#` comments or no label. The messages inside those blocks are not in messages[]. Plain `alt is sick / else is well` and `par Alice to Bob / and Alice to John` do parse as typed fragments, so the opaque blocks are the model's own choice for these statements; reading them would mean parsing source text.
concepts.action: Kept (agentic.mjs sequence view). The 2026-11-14 review (agentic-opaque) confirmed the concept but keyed reasons cut at 160 characters or drawn from an earlier statement listing (without the block's closing lines), so these ten did not match.

concepts.evidence: agentic-mermaid 0.5.6 graph.edges for the test source: e1 { animate: true }, e2 (written `animate: false`) with no animate key, e3 (`animate: true` then `animate: false`) { animate: true }. The edge e2 is identical to an edge with no attachment (`A e1@--> B` alone, and `e1@{ animate: false }` alone), while Mermaid's getData gives false for a written false. The test reads edges[1].animate === false, which the model does not record (and the model's e3 keeps true where Mermaid has false).
concepts.action: Kept (misc.mjs beautifulGraph keeps.animate). The 2026-11-14 review (agentic-edge-animation) disproved the older 'keeps no animation' reason and introduced this one without keying it.

concepts.evidence: XMermaid 0.4.2 state model: transitions are a flat list of { from, to, label } with no document. Every [*] is the one state `__start__`, placed in the composite that writes a [*]: in the test source the root's `[*] --> NotShooting` and the composite's `[*] --> Idle` both start at __start__ (parent '"Not Shooting State" as NotShooting', which XMermaid keeps as the composite's id, apart from a plain state NotShooting). So the root transition is recorded between a composite member and a root state, and which document it was written in is not recorded; the root document's states (getState('NotShooting'), read by the test) depend on it. Where only the root writes a [*], __start__ is root-level (st5-composite-plain); where only the composite does, it is the composite's (st5-composite-start).
concepts.action: Kept (state.mjs stateView). The 2026-11-14 review (state-crossdoc) confirmed it, but the XMermaid key was cut at 160 characters and did not match.

concepts.evidence: beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 and ascii-mermaid 0.1.0: `Class1 -- Class02` and `Class1 --> Class02` both give { from: 'Class1', to: 'Class02', type: 'association', markerAt: 'to' } (no line or link type, no dashed flag), so the test's type1 / type2 'none' and lineType LINE are not recorded. `Class1 .. Class02` gives no relationship at all.
concepts.action: Kept (view-core.mjs zombieClasses). The 2026-11-14 review (class-relation-assoc-others) confirmed it, but keyed both projects with zombie-mermaid's name, which the reason no longer carries.
